analysis.title: #GLOBALMARKETS WEEKLY WRAP-UP, November 07, 2026
key_insights: Chart of the week: INDA (India) ETF and SOX (semiconductor) ETFs moved in an almost perfect inverse relationship during the latest AI selloff (source: TME).

US indexes ended a volatile week lower after Tuesday's midterms, where Democrats gained control of both chambers of Congress. Equities reversed sharply on Thursday on concerns about tighter AI oversight and weak outlooks from major semiconductor companies.

The Nasdaq 100 fell 6.4% and semiconductors fell more than 12% on Thursday, both the worst sessions since March 2020. US stocks partially recovered on Friday. The S&P 500 was down about 2% on the week.
About $2.8 trillion was wiped from US equity market value on Thursday, the largest single-day loss on record. The prior record was $2.69 trillion during the COVID crash.
The VIX gained about +63% as of Nov 5, 2026, the 5th largest VIX jump on record, behind Feb 2007 (+64%) and ahead of Jan 2021 (+62%). The largest is Feb 5, 2018 at +116%.
Options traders are the most bearish since April 2025 after the equity put/call ratio rose to 1. The week included a record put-volume day and a record split between levered and inverse ETF flows.
Morgan Stanley estimates retail investors sold $1.4bn of US equities on Tuesday, their first net sale since April, after buying more than $1 trillion of ETFs and stocks YTD.
The GS high beta momentum basket (GSPRHIMO) is down 51% from its June highs.
Microsoft is reportedly winding down its deal to rent AI cloud capacity from Oracle, as part of a wider reassessment of cloud partnerships.

Semiconductors broke below their 200-day moving average. The S&P 500's 200-day average is holding for now. The Nasdaq bounced off long-term support on Friday, and another sizable drawdown would put that support in question.
Historically, S&P 500 returns were positive in the year after each of three prior times Congress flipped. The sample is small.
Mag7 earnings growth is expected to be overtaken by the other 493 S&P companies for the first time in 4 years this quarter (BlackRock), with base effects and private-investment mark-to-market noted.

Apple beat on revenue and EPS in its fiscal Q4 report. iPhone sales were $57.58B versus $56.48B estimated. Apple was up 4.4% in October while the Nasdaq fell 5%, and its correlation with the Nasdaq has reportedly turned negative.

Anthropic's updated IPO filing reportedly shows Q3 revenue of $17.0B versus $11.6B in Q2, and an operating loss of $567M after a $974M operating profit in Q2. Revenue grew 1,127% y/y versus a 382% rise in compute costs.

Institutional investors are reportedly urging Anthropic to price its IPO at $1.5T to $1.6T, below the roughly $2T discussed earlier. The roadshow may start as soon as next week, with a Nasdaq debut targeted for the week before Thanksgiving (WSJ).
Michael Burry's updated positions: bought more BYD, added Sprouts 2028 calls and JD 2029 calls, and continues to hold Fiserv and PayPal.
Trump Media is down 97% from its peak, with cumulative net losses of $1.8B.

Asian AI-heavy markets have lost about $7 trillion: South Korea -$2.17T (-40% in 4 months), China -$3.01T (-16% in 6 months), Japan -$1.20T (-13.5% in 4+ months), Taiwan -$741B (-16.2% in 1 month). The Kospi had its first death cross since 2024. The Nikkei 225 fell 9.25% on the week.

Per Korean media, Samsung has signed long-term agreements with 10 major customers and is negotiating with 10 more, and its 2027 HBM supply is reportedly sold out. Multiyear commitments improve visibility but do not remove demand, pricing and overcapacity risks.

The October US payrolls report showed +165K versus a 70K median estimate, with prior months revised up. The unemployment rate fell to 4.1% and average hourly earnings rose 0.4% M/M versus 0.3% expected. Money markets priced about 20bps of a December Fed hike.

Treasury yields fell across the curve with short-term yields falling more than long-term yields (steepening), driven by the midterm result and the tech selloff. Strong private payrolls and hawkish Fed comments limited the rally.
Spreads on tech debt are the highest relative to other investment-grade bonds since 2003, as investors demand more premium on AI capex financing.
Brent swung between $97 and $101 on Iran and Strait of Hormuz headlines. WTI settled at $90.83 and Brent at $98.32.
Gold slipped 0.6% to about $4,063 as rate-hike risk returned. The dollar gained and bitcoin weakened.

Texas is central to the AI buildout debate. It is expected to host 25% of data centers coming online through 2030, and Governor Abbott put a moratorium on data center construction on September 21. Investors are weighing the possibility the pause lasts longer after a Democrat won the governorship. Spear's Ivana Delevska argues pushback on data centers predates the election.

A push among some Democrats for a ban on artificial superintelligence is cited as a regulatory risk. An NBC exit poll found AI and data centers were a crucial or major factor for 56% of midterm voters.

Bitcoin was stuck around $75.6K, near where Goldman said its 'Democratic sweep' price would be. A $6.3B Binance hack weighed on sentiment, and 44% of the $6.43B stolen has been frozen or seized (Elliptic).
Kalshi puts the chance of Trump being impeached during his term at 78.5%.

market_movers.rationale: Apple beat on revenue and EPS with iPhone sales of $57.58B versus $56.48B estimated. The stock was up 4.4% in October while the Nasdaq fell 5%.
Microsoft is reportedly winding down its deal to rent AI cloud capacity from Oracle, which pressures neocloud names.
Trump Media is down 97% from its peak and hit another all-time low, with cumulative net losses of $1.8B.

sector_views.rationale: Semis fell more than 12% on Thursday on weak outlooks from major chip companies and AI regulation fears, and broke the 200-day moving average.
BofA calls Texas the most consequential election for data centers, utilities and power this cycle and would carry materially wider volatility margins than the market reflects.
Samsung's 2027 HBM supply is reportedly sold out under long-term agreements, but demand, pricing and overcapacity risks remain.

earnings_insights: Apple reported fiscal Q4 after the bell on Monday and beat on revenue and EPS. iPhone revenue was $57.58B reported versus $56.48B estimate.
Mag7 earnings growth is expected to be overtaken by the other 493 S&P companies for the first time in 4 years this quarter (BlackRock).
Anthropic's reported Q3 revenue was $17.0B versus $11.6B in Q2. Operating loss was $567M versus a $974M operating profit in Q2 (per its reported IPO filing).

macro_indicators.interpretation: A large beat with upward revisions. Goldman's three-month average rose to 137K from 51K, and a December Fed hike is back in play.
The rate fell, supporting hawkish Fed pricing.
Wage growth above expectations supports hawkish pricing.
Money markets price a partial chance of a December rate increase.
Manufacturing has expanded for 10 straight months in 2026.
Input prices came in below expectations but remain elevated.
Brent swung between $97 and $101 on Iran and Hormuz headlines.
Oil fell on the week as markets priced a lower chance of near-term escalation with Iran.
Gold gave back part of its haven bid as rate-hike risk returned.
The dollar rose on the hawkish data.
The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index rose 0.4%.

crypto_views: Bitcoin was around $75.6K, near Goldman's 'Democratic sweep' price level, and weakened on the week.
A $6.3B Binance hack weighed on sentiment. Elliptic says 44% of the $6.43B stolen has been frozen or seized.

geopolitical: US midterms: Democrats took both chambers of Congress, flipping 15 House seats and gaining six Senate seats on net, with high fuel prices and the Iran war weighing on voters.
Iran: Brent swung on reports of tankers hit by mines near the Strait of Hormuz, Trump calling Qatar's Emir about de-escalation, and Bloomberg reporting the US and Iran were edging closer to a deal.
Trump said he will veto legislation from a Democratic Congress.
Bomb threats targeted at least 8 flights across Europe.
British Airways resumed Dubai-London Heathrow flights after an eight-month suspension, while several other airlines keep Dubai routes on hold.
PBOC moved to a new overnight policy rate and injected 541 billion yuan ($81B) on day one, with injections to run daily.
